# Wait for a page that is slow to finish

`isLoaded()` already waits for the URL, the browser's load event (all images, scripts and frames),
the title and the key headings. Some pages keep working after that: a spinner that goes away, a
third-party widget (payments, chat, a form service) that shows up seconds later. A test that clicks
before then fails, or passes by luck.

Add proof to the page's **load-checks** YOURS block, at the end of `isLoaded()`:

```java
        // ==== YOURS (load-checks): ...
        if (!WaitActions.waitForInvisibilityOf(page, HomeElements.LOADING_SPINNER)) {
            throw new AssertionError(name() + " did not load! LOADING_SPINNER never went away!");
        }
        if (!WaitActions.waitForVisibilityOf(page, HomeElements.PAYMENT_FRAME, 15_000)) {
            throw new AssertionError(name() + " did not load! PAYMENT_FRAME did not show within 15 s!");
        }
        // ==== END YOURS (load-checks) ====
```

- Wait for the **last** thing to arrive, and for the **spinner to go**, not for time to pass.
- Give a slow third-party widget its own longer limit (the last argument, in milliseconds).
- Each check throws an Error that says which element, so a failure explains itself.
- Everything slow on this site (every page is): raise `-DpageLoadTimeout` / `-DelementTimeout`
  when running, rather than in code.
